facts.title: Business Integra Technology Solutions, Inc.
facts.solicitation: RFP No. 25R5032 for security, information technology (IT), and other support services
facts.procurement_type: Negotiated procurement; cost-plus-fixed-fee contract with a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods
facts.est_value: Not stated in the decision; evaluated costs were $166,226,487 (Business Integra) and $185,344,992 (HII)
facts.evaluation_scheme: Best-value tradeoff considering security and general services, IT, past performance, and cost
facts.background: On May 12, 2025, the Navy issued the RFP seeking security, IT, and general services at six U.S. locations. The solicitation contemplated a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract with a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. Award was to be made on a best-value tradeoff basis considering security and general services, IT, past performance, and cost. Proposals were rated outstanding, good, acceptable, marginal, or unacceptable, and a proposal had to be rated at least acceptable to be eligible for award. The Navy received four proposals by the July 14 closing date, including proposals from Business Integra and HII. The source selection authority agreed with the advisory council's recommendations and found HII's higher-cost proposal to represent the best value. The Navy notified Business Integra of the award to HII and later provided a debriefing. Business Integra then filed this protest.

protester_grounds.claim: The Navy unreasonably assessed significant weaknesses under the security staffing approach subfactor, including its ACSO staffing, organizational structure and reporting, pre-vetted staff deployment, and security manager resume, and applied unstated criteria.
The Navy unreasonably found the general services scenario response unrealistic, arbitrarily and without adequate documentation.

The Navy unreasonably assessed a significant weakness under the security technical approach subfactor by reading the proposal's description of the security support program manager's duties as direct work rather than supervision.
The Navy unreasonably evaluated the IT factor and the best-value tradeoff, and the agency's evaluation was otherwise flawed.

facts.agency_position: The Navy argues its evaluation was reasonable and consistent with the solicitation's criteria. It states the protester's proposal was internally inconsistent on ACSO staffing, lacked explanation of its organizational reporting, and did not address SCI and SAP access in its hiring approach. The Navy also argues the scenario schedule was unrealistic and that the protester's proposal described the program manager performing tasks the PWS assigned to supervision.
facts.record_facts_protected: Business Integra was rated marginal under security and general services and under IT, with marginal ratings for security technical approach, security staffing approach, and general services scenario response, and an acceptable rating for the security scenario response. HII was rated good under security and general services and outstanding under IT. The evaluators found Business Integra's proposal stated five ACSOs while its organizational chart identified only three full-time equivalent ACSO positions. The security manager's resume referenced SAPs only in a requirements table, without specifying the role, and the evaluators found the older experience could be irrelevant given policy changes. The source selection authority concluded that Business Integra's proposal included significant flaws showing a high likelihood of unsuccessful performance, and that awarding to it would place the program at risk for a savings of $19 million.

outcome.remedy: None; the protest was denied and no recommendation was made.
